place.explore: A mountain village in southern Kyrgyzstan. On 10 October 2026 the slope above it gave way.
place.research: Study window ~5 × 5 km around the slide. Event date from local reports; scar outline mapped on post-event optical imagery.

rain.explore: It rained hard for a week before the slope failed. Water makes soil heavy and weak.
rain.research: GPM IMERG Late daily totals over the window. One IMERG pixel is ~10 km, larger than the slope, so this is regional rain, not rain on the slide itself.

radar.explore: The satellite sends its own radio waves, so it sees the ground through clouds and at night. After the slide, the broken ground echoes back differently.
radar.research: L-band HH brightens where fresh debris adds roughness; HV darkens where vegetation volume was removed. InSAR coherence collapses across the scar in the pair spanning the event.

tracking.explore: Each NISAR pass is one frame. Press Play to watch the slope change pass by pass.
tracking.research: Line-of-sight displacement from GUNW pairs, referenced to a stable area and masked where coherence < 0.3. LOS is not downslope motion.

exposure.explore: These are the houses and roads closest to the slide.
exposure.research: Buildings and roads from OpenStreetMap within 2 km of the scar centre. Proximity is not a hazard assessment.

layers.title: Coherence
layers.description: How alike two passes are. Low = the surface was disturbed (or snow, or vegetation).

layers.title: Displacement (LOS)
layers.description: Movement towards or away from the satellite between two passes. Blank where coherence is too low to trust.

layers.title: Optical
layers.description: Ordinary colour picture for reference. Clouds hide the ground on some dates; radar sees through them.

exposure.method: OpenStreetMap buildings and road length within 2 km of the scar centre. Not a hazard or population estimate.

validation.method: |ΔHH| > 3 dB between the last pass before and the first pass after the event; radar blind spots excluded. Threshold tuned on the stable reference area.

limitations: Radar cannot see layover/shadow areas on steep slopes (grey on the map).
Snow from late October lowers coherence and changes backscatter on high ground; do not read it as slope movement.
Fast landslide motion decorrelates InSAR, so displacement is meaningful before and after the event, not during it.
Line-of-sight displacement is not the same as downslope displacement.
IMERG rain is regional (~10 km pixels).
